chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of several others that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The khums is levied on five things: on treasures, mines, diving (for pearls), and booties. Ibn Abi Umayr forgot the fifth.

The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: I think the fifth item which Ibn Abi Umayr forgot is wealth that a man inherits, and he knows that it contains both halal and haram, but he does not know the owners of the haram portion to pay it to them, nor does he know the haram specifically to avoid it; therefore, he pays the khums from it.
ai.seo_question: What are the five items subject to khums and how is inherited mixed wealth handled?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the four primary categories of khums while noting the compiler's scholarly deduction that the fifth category is mixed inheritance (al-mal al-mukhtalat) where the haram portion cannot be distinguished. This specific ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of paying khums as a precautionary measure when the exact haram share is unknown, ensuring the purification of the inherited wealth. The inclusion of 'sea diving' (al-ghaws) reflects the historical economic context of pearl diving in the Persian Gulf, which was a significant source of wealth for early Shia communities.
